title: EDT, Git and collaboration
goal: Organize source in EDT/Git with review and reproducible builds without secrets or infobase overwrites.
prerequisites: onec.p11; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Distinguish configuration source from infobase data and preserve them separately.
Read git diff, record one change and identify the exact commit SHA.
Check the configuration in a new infobase and state the EDT result separately.
sections: Configuration source describes objects, attributes and handlers. Infobase data consists of particular customers, requests and entered values. Git stores and compares versions of text source; it does not automatically back up every infobase record. This exercise therefore produces two separate items: a source directory for Git and a DT backup containing the accepted infobase state.

Distinguish Designer XML/BSL exports, an EDT project and an infobase containing data. Renaming a directory converts none of these formats. Complete the available Designer/Git route first. EDT is an additional development environment whose compatibility with the installed platform must be checked separately.

A branch is a separate line of changes in a Git repository. A commit records a set of changes; its SHA identifies that exact commit. The git diff command shows changes since the recorded version. Read those differences before committing instead of treating a successful command as proof of correct behavior.

Change just one hint that belongs to your application. Record where it appears and its original wording. The same workflow should then display the revised wording while objects, customer references and request data remain intact. Unexpected object deletions or replacement UUIDs indicate a different change that needs investigation.
How to build a verifiable new infobase

A working directory may include edits not recorded in a commit. Run git status --short before testing; empty output means Git sees no uncommitted changes to tracked files or untracked files. Record git rev-parse HEAD and the platform version so another reviewer can identify the source actually tested.

Create a new empty teaching infobase and load the exported configuration files through Designer. Check the configuration, update the database configuration and start Enterprise. Find the changed hint. Source files do not transfer records from the accepted infobase: verify data preservation separately by restoring its DT into another empty infobase. These are separate checks.

A conflict means two changes cannot be combined automatically. Preserve both versions, identify the behavior required by each, produce a combined version and rerun both checks. Blindly keeping one side can discard a requirement from the other. First practise this reasoning on a copy of your own text description, retaining the originals.

If EDT is installed, record its version, the platform version and the supported import route; then verify an actual build of your own project. If EDT is absent or compatibility is untested, mark EDT NOT RUN. The observed Designer/Git result remains valid within its own scope.

examples.title: Git inspection commands — terminal commands, not BSL
examples.source:
git status --short
git diff
git log -1 --oneline
git rev-parse HEAD
examples.expected: File state, differences and the last commit identifier are visible.
examples.explanation: Read file membership and differences first. Record the full SHA after committing and load that exact source into the new infobase.
trace: Checks application behavior as well as the Git operation.

examples.title: Why a directory name does not prove compatibility
examples.source:
Designer XML/BSL → supported loading → new infobase
EDT project → supported EDT import → separate build check
examples.expected: Renaming a directory without importing does not count as EDT verification.
examples.explanation: Content and the supported loading process determine the format. One environment does not prove another works.
trace: EDT has not imported and built the project

lab.title: EDT, Git and collaboration
lab.environment: Separate own synthetic infobase; retain the prior module and its backup. Studio and Sandbox optional.
steps: Close Enterprise for your accepted infobase. In Designer choose Administration → Dump infobase (Администрирование → Выгрузить информационную базу) and save a DT outside the source directory. Use Configuration → Dump configuration to files (Конфигурация → Выгрузить конфигурацию в файлы) into a new empty directory. Record the infobase, backup and source locations.

Open a terminal in that new source directory. Run git init and git switch -c feature/minutes-hint. Read git status --short: include only your own XML/BSL and study documentation. Run git add -- ., read git diff --cached, then record the baseline with git commit -m "Сохранить исходную учебную конфигурацию". This local exercise needs no remote server.

Change one of your hints, review git diff and commit the separate change. Record git rev-parse HEAD. In a new empty infobase use Designer → Configuration → Load configuration from files (Конфигурация → Загрузить конфигурацию из файлов). Load the recorded sources, check the configuration, press F7 and then F5. Find the revised hint in Enterprise.

Retain both commits and the before/after comparison. Restore the DT into another empty infobase and verify earlier requests separately. Review the supplied two-version text case, preserve both versions and explain the merge. Record whether EDT was actually tested; mark it NOT RUN if unavailable.
expected: DT and source are separate; the accepted infobase remains intact.
The first commit contains only your own teaching sources and its SHA is recorded.
The new infobase uses the stated commit and shows only the intended hint change.
Both versions, the data-restoration result and the separate EDT status are retained.
evidence: Exact own source and version; actual keys, observations and expected versus actual table.
Original and changed-copy results, failed attempts and untested environment limits.
lab.negative: Two copies of a description are supplied: one clarifies the action and the other adds the expected result. Explain why keeping only one loses a requirement. Produce a combined description and retain both originals.

mistakes: Success is inferred from an unavailable environment.
Separate actual observations from a planned advanced scenario and name edition limits.
A failed attempt is removed to make the record look successful.
Retain the original failure, its cause, correction and regression evidence.
An own-copy change is applied over the accepted original.
Verify the actual directory and preserve source identities before making changes.

quiz.question: Should metadata conflicts always use new UUIDs?

review: Tool version and build route are documented.
Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
